text: Single-task results. We fine-tune a separate policy for each HumanoidArena task, comparing two
initialization strategies. Kimodo-Policy is fine-tuned directly on task data, whereas Kimodo-Policy ∗
initializes ControlNet and the hand head from our 419-hour VLA policy-pretraining stage. RTC is
disabled for both variants to match the reported baselines. Kimodo-Policy achieves the highest over-
all success rate (SR; 69.51%), exceeding DP (Chi et al., 2023), the strongest baseline (60.0%), by
9.51 percentage points. It also attains the lowest average fall rate (AFR; 4.29%, tied with Kimodo-
Policy ∗ ) and highest average SR on human–scene interaction (HSI; 84.58%). Kimodo-Policy ∗
achieves 67.14% overall SR and 84.17% HSI SR, with the highest task-level SRs on OpenDoor
(93.3%) and VisNavi (76.7%). The framework supports language-conditioned whole-body control:
VLA pretraining improves selected tasks, whereas direct fine-tuning yields higher overall SR.
Multi-task results. We jointly train one policy on all seven HumanoidArena tasks and evaluate it
in the SONIC-based setting (Wang et al., 2026a; Luo et al., 2026), with RTC disabled to match
the baseline protocol. In Table 2, Kimodo-Policy ∗ achieves 72.14% overall SR, exceeding the
strongest baseline, π 0.5 (Black et al., 2025a) (53.8%), by 18.33 percentage points, with the low-
est AFR (4.29%). It attains the highest mean SRs for human–object interaction (HOI; 56.11%) and
human–scene interaction (HSI; 84.17%), and leads on P&Pbox (90.0%), OpenDoor (95.0%), Sit-
Sofa (96.7%, tied), and VisNavi (76.7%). Without VLA pretraining, Kimodo-Policy obtains 67.63%
overall SR and 51.67% HOI SR, a decrease of only 1.88 percentage points in overall SR relative to
single-task training. Thus, one shared policy can retain much of the task-specific performance across
seven skills, with high success and low fall rates.
